_doc: The FlatBars editor token vocabulary — ADR-017's single source of truth, the
ONE contract shared by the three consumers it names: the engine `tokenize`
API (whose `kind` strings are the keys below), the `flatbars-lsp` semantic-
token legend (built from the `lsp` mappings), and the TextMate fallback
grammar (`editors/flatbars.tmLanguage.json`).
The fallback grammar is the well-known Handlebars TextMate grammar, re-
identified as `source.flatbars` and extended to cover all four dialects
(inverse sections, Mustache inheritance `{{<}}`/`{{$}}`, set delimiters, and
MaxBars operators). We keep its standard scope names (`keyword.control.*`,
`support.function.*`, `string.quoted.*`, …) on purpose: themes already colour
them, so FlatBars looks like the Handlebars developers know. The grammar
colours ONLY template syntax plus a leading YAML front-matter block (`---`);
host text (HTML, etc.) is left plain, since a FlatBars template's output is not
necessarily HTML. Every FlatBars tag scope ends in `.handlebars` — that suffix
is how the gate tells a tag from content.
Because the grammar is RICHER than the engine (it splits a tag into sigil /
name / args / literals, where the engine paints one kind per tag), the drift
gate does NOT assert a scope==kind bijection. `check:tmgrammar` asserts, per
dialect, that the grammar agrees with the engine on (1) TAG BOUNDARIES (which
characters are inside a FlatBars tag) and (2) LITERAL positions (string /
number). Everything else is allowed enrichment — the fallback is the floor,
the LSP is the authority. `check:highlight` still pins what the engine emits.
`role`: `tag` (a whole-tag span) or `interior` (a literal/operator carved
inside a tag). `lsp.type`/`lsp.modifiers` are the semantic-token legend entry.
`tmScopes` are the grammar scopes that express this kind; `[]` means the
stateless fallback gives up (the LSP corrects it). Only the `string`/`number`
scopes are gate-checked as literals; the tag scopes are documentation.
`lspEmitKinds` is the SPARSE set of kinds the LSP semantic-token layer emits.
Semantic tokens are CORRECTIONS over the rich TextMate floor, not a blanket
re-colour: the LSP emits only where it knows something the stateless grammar
cannot — dialect-scoped interior operators/literals, set delimiters, and
dialect-disallowed errors. For the structural tags (interpolation, raw, blocks,
partials, comments) the grammar already paints the familiar Handlebars look
(braces vs name), so the LSP stays SILENT and lets it show through, rather than
flattening `{{{x}}}` to one whole-tag colour. (Trade-off: a set-delimiter
SWITCH's following tags are not semantic-corrected — a rare, documented give-up.)

set-delimiter.description: {{=A B=}} — a set-delimiter directive. The DIRECTIVE is coloured; the stateless fallback cannot track the new delimiters that follow it (the LSP does).

error.description: A structurally-valid tag the dialect disallows. DIALECT-DEPENDENT: the stateless fallback paints the shape as valid; only the LSP knows the dialect.

string.description: A quoted string literal inside a tag.

number.description: A numeric literal inside a tag.

operator.description: An infix/prefix operator inside a tag (MaxBars). Coloured as enrichment; not gate-checked, since the engine only carves operators under MaxBars' infixArith.
